examples.problem_statement: The number of years it would take for the value of an investment to double, at 26% interest compounded annually, is approximately

solution.result: 1 grows by a factor of 1.26 each year and must reach 2
solution.description: Set up the model the book uses: begin with one dollar and multiply by 1.26 for each year that passes, since doubling means reaching two dollars.
Apply the multiplier once to get the end-of-Year-1 value; it is still below the doubling target.
Multiply the Year 1 value by 1.26 again to get the end-of-Year-2 value, which is still short of 2.

solution.result: 2.000376 at the end of Year 3, which is about 2.00
solution.description: Multiply the Year 2 value by 1.26 a third time; the result is approximately 2.00, so the doubling target is reached here.
Read off the first year whose ending value meets the target: the investment takes 3 years to double.

key_reminders: Compounding multiplies the previous year's amount by 1 + r each year, so carry the running value forward.
Doubling means the running value reaches 2 times the starting amount.
Compounded growth earns interest on the interest, so it doubles faster than simple interest suggests.
common_mistakes: Treating 26% as simple interest and reasoning that 26% is a bit more than 25% = 1/4, which wrongly gives about 4 years instead of 3.
Stopping at Year 2 because 1.5876 looks close to 2, when the target is not yet reached.

concept.technique_name: HCF of quantities after unit conversion

examples.problem_statement: Find the greatest weight which can be contained exactly in 1 kg 235 gm and 3 kg 430 gm.

solution.description: Reduce the first quantity to a single unit by converting the kilogram part to grams and adding the gram part.
Reduce the second quantity to grams the same way, so both weights are expressed in the same unit.
Take the HCF of the two gram values, because the greatest weight contained exactly in both must divide both.

key_reminders: Both quantities must be expressed in the same unit before any HCF is taken.
The greatest measure contained exactly in two quantities is their HCF.
common_mistakes: Taking the HCF of 235 and 430 alone and ignoring the kilogram parts, instead of using 1235 and 3430.
Taking the LCM instead of the HCF, which asks for the smallest common multiple rather than the greatest common measure.

examples.problem_statement: Compare the rates of two trains, one travelling at 45 km an hour and the other at 10 m a second.

solution.description: Convert the second train's speed from metres per second to kilometres per hour by multiplying by the factor 18/5.

solution.result: the two speeds are 45 km/hr and 36 km/hr
solution.description: State both rates in the same unit so they can be compared directly.
Form the ratio of the two km/hr figures and reduce it by dividing both terms by 9.

key_reminders: Multiply by 18/5 to convert metres per second into kilometres per hour.
Rates can only be compared as a ratio once both are in the same unit.
Reduce the resulting ratio to lowest terms.
common_mistakes: Using 5/18 instead of 18/5 and converting in the wrong direction, turning 10 m/s into a much smaller km/hr figure.
Comparing 45 with 10 directly and reporting 9 : 2 without converting units.
